title: The Guy Who Studies Too
description:
He ran into Hyunsu again in the shared kitchen.

Ramen again. 2 AM again.

"You prepping for something, too?"

Four years into the Grade 9 civil service exam. This year was his last shot, he said.
His face was exhausted but not surrendered.

choices.result_text:
"You'll get it this year."

Hyunsu smiled. A real one.
"You'll be fine too, hyung."

{name} held onto that longer than expected.

"Yeah. But quitting now feels like I'd regret it longer."

{name} understood that.

Choosing a different path versus staying on this one — you only know which was right later.

title: Exam Day
description:
Hyunsu left at 5 AM.

{name} half-woke to the sound of the door, then closed his eyes again.

Today was the exam. Grade 9 administrative track.

choices.result_text:
Hyunsu came back in the evening.
"How'd it go?"

He paused before answering.
"I think it went okay. Maybe."

Maybe. That one word carried a lot.

choices.text: Say nothing — better not to press
choices.result_text:
Hyunsu came back quietly.
{name} caught his eye in the hallway and asked without words.
Hyunsu gave a small nod. A signal that said: I'm okay.

title: Hyunsu Passed
description:
Hyunsu knocked on his door.

"Hyung, I passed."

He said it quietly. No shouting, no celebration.
Four years of weight in his voice.

choices.result_text:
"Seriously? That's great."

Hyunsu smiled — the first real smile {name} had seen from him.

{name} felt good about it. Like it was his own.

When someone else's success feels like yours — that's what a real connection is.

title: Hyunsu Didn't Pass
description:
Hyunsu came back late that night.

He didn't say anything. {name} could tell from the way he moved.

The results were out.

choices.text: Sit with him for a while
choices.result_text:
They sat in the shared kitchen without speaking.

No ramen this time.

Sometimes being present is the only thing you can offer.
{name} didn't have any words. Neither did Hyunsu.

They sat until past midnight.

{name} went back to his room.

Some things need to be processed alone.
He knew that.

The wall between the rooms was thin. Neither of them slept well that night.

title: Hyunsu's New Direction
description:
Hyunsu said he was moving out.

He was quitting the civil service exam to prepare for a job.
His major had been accounting. He was going to start studying for the CPA again.

"It's not farther, and it's not closer. It's just a different road."

{name} turned those words over for a long time.

choices.result_text:
"You'll do great."

Hyunsu smiled. A firmer smile this time.

Choosing a different road and giving up are not the same thing.
{name} learned that from Hyunsu.

title: Running Into Hyunsu Again
description:
A KakaoTalk message. It was Hyunsu.

"Hyung, I got hired at an accounting firm."

A photo came through. A suit. A business card.

{name} looked at the photo for a long while.

choices.result_text:
"Wait, for real? That's amazing!!"

"It's thanks to you, hyung. For knocking on my door back then."

{name} set the phone down.

Five years in Seoul. Some days, a message like this arrives.

title: Hyunsu's Posting
description:
Hyunsu was packing boxes.

"Hyung, I got my posting. I have to go next week."

Some county office in Gyeonggi-do. After four years, he was leaving the goshiwon.

Two boxes. Exam prep books. A calendar.
All that time in this room fit into two boxes.

choices.result_text:
A nearby sundae gukbap place. Hyunsu ate a lot.

"When are you getting out of here, hyung?"
"...Not sure yet."

Hyunsu just smiled. That smile stayed with {name} a while.
Same starting line — and one of them had crossed it first.

choices.text: Tell him it's great news. Say goodbye.
choices.result_text:
"Good for you. Take care of yourself out there."
"Thank you, hyung."

The room was empty the next day.
The shared kitchen — one ramen pot missing —
looked, somehow, bigger than before.
